analysis.session_summary: The weekend tape was quiet and mostly missing hard catalysts: event reactions were empty and nearly every zigzag leg had no clear cause. USD selling was rejected and the dollar closed firmer, while JPY was the weakest major and CHF gave back an early bid. Risk appetite improved at the margin with VIX/USD down -3.903% and USD/JPY up 47.7 pips, though EUR/USD barely moved with a 2.2-pip loss. The only calendar item ahead is US CB Consumer Confidence, which can reset the dollar tone.

themes.evidence: VIX/USD fell -3.903% to 19.084; USD/JPY rallied 47.7 pips to 157.414; Brent/USD moved erratically but no new negative headline.
USD strength 0.112% after intraday trough -0.091%; DXY/USD closed +0.081%.

themes.theme: No macro catalyst for most pair moves
themes.evidence: Legs repeatedly show confidence none, cause null, or nearest item too weak; event_reactions array is empty.

currency_drivers.USD: Early selling rejected and closed firmer; no US data or rate driver in window.
currency_drivers.EUR: Held its range near highs; no euro-area catalyst, only brief France Moody's headline support.
currency_drivers.JPY: Led +0.06% then gave back 88%; closed weakest; no Japanese catalyst.
currency_drivers.GBP: Sold to -0.097%, recovered 72%; no UK catalyst in window.
currency_drivers.AUD: Sold to -0.149%, recovered 66%; no Australian catalyst.
currency_drivers.CAD: Closed at its best after WSJ report on removing Canadian tariffs; no domestic data.
currency_drivers.CHF: Led +0.146% then gave back 98%; no Swiss catalyst.
currency_drivers.NZD: Sold to -0.235%, recovered 74%; no New Zealand catalyst.

leg_notes.EUR/USD: A Lescure-driven early bounce gave way to a no-catalyst fade into 14:45, then a final 16.6-pip bounce left it 2.2 pips lower with no single dominant driver.

scenarios.name: Pre-CB USD drift holds
scenarios.thesis: Without a hard catalyst, the dollar's recovered bid persists; JPY stays weakest and EUR/USD remains pinned near 1.11911.
triggers: US CB Consumer Confidence prints at or above 81.2 forecast
scenarios.invalidation: EUR/USD closes above 1.11911 while USD/JPY breaks below 157.414.

pair_paths.rationale: Repeating the session's 52.7-pip range with USD firm and no euro catalyst.
Carry/FX risk bid; USD/JPY sees similar 98.9-pip range as yen stays weakest.
Sterling fades after early recovery; its session range was 59.5 pips.

scenarios.name: US data miss triggers reversal
scenarios.thesis: A weak CB Consumer Confidence reading challenges the dollar recovery and lifts oversold yen and Swiss franc.
scenarios.invalidation: USD/JPY closes above 157.414 and VIX stays below 19.084.

pair_paths.rationale: Full session range reversal in a safe-haven bid; 98.9 was the day's range.
Dollar retreat allows EUR/USD to retrace its 52.7-pip session range.
CHF recovers from its rejected bid; 47.2 was the session range.

scenarios.name: Risk-on accelerates after clean close
scenarios.thesis: Lower VIX and no new escalation extend carry and commodity FX strength, while USD gives up early gains except against JPY.
scenarios.invalidation: VIX/USD reverses above 19.084 or USD/CAD recaptures 1.40123.

pair_paths.rationale: NZD selling rejected, could recover full 37.2-pip range in risk-on extension.
GBP also sold off and recovered 72%; a risk-on break retraces the 59.5-pip range.
Tariff relief supports CAD; 71.4-pip range is the measured session band.

risks.why_it_matters: It is the only scheduled USD release in the window and can reverse the dollar recovery.
France Moody's headline earlier gave only brief support; no hard catalysts, so any new geopolitical headline can dominate.
risks.watch: Iran/Middle East and tariff headlines from WSJ/Trump.

risks.why_it_matters: Many legs had no clear cause and confidence none; flow can exaggerate moves.
risks.watch: EUR/USD range 52.7 and USD/JPY 98.9 as measured band.

analysis.calendar_ahead_note: CB Consumer Confidence is the only scheduled item; a print below the 81.2 forecast or 81.9 previous can challenge the dollar recovery.
